customer_jobs.definition: Functional, social, and emotional tasks the procurement entity is performing

types.functional: Infrastructure modernization, system integration, service delivery improvement
types.social: Demonstrating fiscal responsibility, stakeholder confidence, regulatory compliance
types.emotional: Mitigating political risk, career protection, organizational reputation

customer_jobs.proposal_application: Identifies the fundamental objective — anchor ALL messaging to these jobs

customer_pains.definition: Negative emotions, undesired costs, and severe obstacles the customer experiences
customer_pains.ranking_rule: Rank by intensity — address highest-impact vulnerabilities FIRST
customer_pains.proposal_application: Maps directly to risk mitigation strategy in technical volume

customer_gains.definition: Tangible benefits the customer uses to measure success
customer_gains.proposal_application: Informs ROI calculations and defines success metrics in executive summary

pain_relievers.definition: Explicit explanations of how proposed methodology alleviates specific frustrations
pain_relievers.rule: Translate generic features into SPECIFIC remedies for RECOGNIZED bottlenecks
pain_relievers.anti_pattern: Never describe a feature without connecting it to a diagnosed pain

gain_creators.definition: Demonstrations of how offering produces outcomes the customer desires
gain_creators.rule: Focus on aspects that EXCEED baseline RFP requirements
gain_creators.proposal_application: Highlights added value — the discriminator in competitive evaluation

value_proposition_canvas.fit_test: Product-market fit achieved when every Pain has a Reliever and every Gain has a Creator

jtbd_framework.purpose: Ensures messaging connects specific technical features to measurable business outcomes
jtbd_framework.risk_mitigated: Internal misalignment where sales, marketing, and proposal teams describe value differently

application.step_1: Identify the core job the customer is hiring the solution to do
application.step_2: Map desired outcomes (metrics the customer uses to judge success)
application.step_3: Align every proposal section to these outcomes, not to internal capabilities

customer_value_consistency_canvas.foundation: Service-Dominant Logic — value is co-created with the user

structure.as_is: Customer's current state — document operational reality, pain intensity, unmet needs
structure.to_be: Customer's desired achievement status — measurable outcomes, KPIs, strategic vision

customer_value_consistency_canvas.proposal_role: Bridge the gap between AS-IS and TO-BE — the proposal IS the bridge narrative

chain.feature: A technical capability or attribute of the solution
chain.advantage: Why the feature is superior to alternatives or the status quo
chain.benefit: The specific, measurable outcome the customer gains from this advantage

examples.bad: We have 15 years of experience in petrochemical EPC projects
examples.good: Our 15-year track record in petrochemical EPC (feature) has refined a proprietary risk model that identifies schedule threats 6 weeks earlier than industry standard (advantage), reducing your project delivery risk by 40% and protecting your timeline commitments (benefit)

feature_advantage_benefit.rule: Every claim in the proposal MUST complete the full F→A→B chain or be deleted
